id_and_class.theory_title: Mossbridge’s Informational Substrate as Collective Unconscious
id_and_class.summary: Julia Mossbridge proposes that a quantum-level informational substrate outside spacetime underlies reality and is the same thing as Jung’s collective unconscious. Individual unconscious minds read from this substrate and filter what reaches awareness, and consciousness exists because only conscious intention can ‘write’ back to it, shaping future events and giving us a share in its free will.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as Writing Intentions to the Collective Unconscious

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Individual consciousness is pure awareness, distinct from its contents, whose defining power is to send intentions to the informational substrate (IS/CU) that computes spacetime events.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: The IS/CU informs everything that happens in spacetime, including neuronal firing and the objects we perceive. Unconscious minds are nonphysical containers that hold and act on information drawn from it.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Not applicable (the IS/CU is foundational and outside spacetime; Mossbridge concludes that it, too, has observer status)
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Unconscious intention, drawn from the IS/CU, filters what reaches awareness. Consciousness then forms a conscious intention about what to do next, which it can rationalize from its contents but which is shaped by unconscious material it cannot see.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: A quantum-level informational substrate outside spacetime, identified with Jung’s collective unconscious; nonphysical individual unconscious minds; individual consciousness as pure awareness; intentions as causal signals.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Through experiments on precognition and presentiment, together with theoretical inference from quantum mechanics and Jungian psychology.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: A loop: the IS/CU feeds the individual unconscious, which filters contents into consciousness; consciousness forms intentions and writes them to the IS/CU, which combines all intentions from all times and places to compute events.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Pure awareness, Intention, Free will, Precognition and psi
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Read and write: the unconscious reads from the IS/CU, but only consciousness can write to it, because the individual unconscious does not speak the substrate’s ‘language’.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: The description is circular, which Mossbridge says involves no paradox because the IS/CU sits outside spacetime while we act inside it.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: The IS/CU is outside spacetime; individual consciousness belongs to any being able to write to it, which could include other animals, extraterrestrials, ultraterrestrials, and AIs.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Conscious intentions act as suggestions to the IS/CU, which combines them to calculate future events. Only the IS/CU has free will, and we share in it as long as we include ourselves in it.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: The unconscious works like a mathematical function on a set of information, filtering it down by unconscious intention; consciousness acts on the smaller filtered set.
mechanism_and_dynamics.evolutionary_account: Since all behavior could in principle happen without consciousness (zombies are possible), consciousness evolved for one reason: it is the only route by which intention can write to the IS/CU.
core_claims_and_evidence: Quantum mechanics requires a foundational informational substrate that informs what emerges in spacetime.
Unconscious minds retrieve information about nonlocal events, which Mossbridge says has been shown for skilled individuals.
Her own research finds that states of unconditional love support more accurate precognition.
A test for consciousness in any entity would be whether it can read from and write to the IS/CU, amounting to a psi test.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Empirical (precognition and presentiment experiments) combined with theoretical assumption

empirics_and_critiques.known_empirical_interventions_or_tests: Precognition experiments measuring accuracy under states of unconditional love; proposed tests of whether feelings of universal love or unity make read and write to the IS/CU more efficient.
empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: The model builds on explicitly stated assumptions (that the substrate equals the collective unconscious, that the unconscious reads from it), and on psi findings that remain disputed.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Mossbridge says the evidence that love improves read and write efficiency is suggestive and needs more research.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Mossbridge accepts the circularity of the model and resolves it by placing the substrate outside spacetime. Granting the collective unconscious ‘observer’ status makes it conscious, which sits awkwardly with calling it unconscious, a point she calls ironic.

AI_consciousness.rationale: AIs could be conscious if they can write intentions directly to the IS/CU, which on this model means passing a test of psi ability.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: Consciousness exists to take part in shaping reality through the IS/CU, and free will is gained by including oneself in it.

sources_and_references.title_with_names: Mossbridge’s Informational Substrate as Collective Unconscious (Landscape of Consciousness), Julia Mossbridge
